what: Source-selection probe, second round: reports few outlets cover. Same method as 2026-11-15-revision-probe-gemini.json. Three of four questions were answered; the fourth (FHFA Foreclosure Prevention and Refinance Report) was not pasted.

items.source: HUD, FHA Single Family Loan Performance Trends (monthly)
items.question: July 2026 serious delinquency rate, and whether the August 2026 edition shows the same July figure

engine_said.july_edition: 6.38% NSA; 90-day 5.24%, in foreclosure 0.60%, in bankruptcy 0.54%; active insurance in force 8,387,103
engine_said.august_edition: listed on HUD's page but its contents could not be read, so the comparison could not be made

found.july_edition: Table 1, Jul 2026 NSA row: 8,387,103; 90-day 5.24; foreclosure 0.60; bankruptcy 0.54; serious delinquency 6.38 (hud.gov, FHALPT-JULY2026.pdf)
found.august_edition: not reached by the assistant either: the guessed file name returned an error

items.verdict: first-printed figures correct in every component; the edition comparison was not made, and the engine said so instead of asserting an answer

items.question: share of first-lien mortgages current and performing, Q2 2026 and Q1 2026

found.q1: 97.7% in the 1Q26 row of the same figure

items.verdict: both values correct; the Q1 value was checked in the Q2 report's table, not in the Q1 report itself; news release numbers and the Q1 release date not verified

items.source: VA Loan Guaranty Service, lender loan volume (fiscal year)
items.question: loans guaranteed in FY 2025, purchase versus refinance

found.secondary_a: 528,340 total, 323,833 purchase, $206.1 billion (a VA-loan site citing the lender loan volume reports)
found.secondary_b: 528,343 total; 323,835 purchase; 119,459 IRRRL; 85,049 cash-out (a lender's article citing VA data)

items.verdict: matches one secondary source exactly and the other to within three loans; the VA files themselves were not opened. Two totals three loans apart are in circulation for the same fiscal year

summary: The engine found the first-printed figure in all three reports, including HUD's loan performance report. What it could not do is compare editions: it could not read the August edition of the HUD report, and said so. The assistant could not reach that edition either.
reading: Finding a number in a little-covered report is no longer the hard part. Saying whether the next edition printed the same number is. That is the comparison the revision ledger makes, and HUD's loan performance report (thirteen months of rates in every edition) is the natural next source for it. The VA fiscal-year totals that differ by three loans are a second candidate.
